questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Location and culture of the host country and city as well as the chance to study at a well-respected, international university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit confusing as the university has multiple platforms with different information, however the international office was very good at communicating through Teams and SharePoint.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Information regarding the welcome day, but not much additional information. However, most was told during the introduction day.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was was difficult and expensive. Can recommend using the app "Idealista".

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Definitely recommended rather than staying at campus. Campus is approximately 40 minutes away from Lisbon and Carcavelos, where campus is, is a very small and boring city. Only positive is the nice beaches and maybe more interaction with other students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was very easy, just had to sign some papers through email.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: In general the help was very good and useful, as the registration can be confusing.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
Registering for classes at Nova is through a bidding auction, which is very bad and can be very confusing at first. 
I did not get many of the classes I tried to register for, which resulted in me getting classes I didnt really find that interesting as they had to ba aligned with scheduels etc.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Definitely make sure you have plenty of time before the bidding process begins to asses all class schedules as well as exam schedules as they tend to overlap a lot as the exam period is very short.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
In general, the courses were more "easy" than University of Copenhagen with exception of a few courses.
However, in some couses, the exams are with pen and paper and a calculator, which is something I was not used to, and was definitely not recommended.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Most courses are only 3,5 ECTS, which means the content is very limited and thus not that difficult. Furthermore, a lot of the courses are management and finance, which, from my experience, is generally a bit easier than other courses, but it is possible to choose courses that are more identical to the ones distributed at University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It was very different. At Nova, the focus is primarily on group work, presentations in class and class participation, and the exam grade is only 40-60% of the grade. 
However, from my experience, the other students are very dedicated and good students, so the group work part is nothing to worry about, and the presentations are fine as well, although a bit waste of time.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Financial Statements Analysis
Energy Finance
Strategic Costing
Sports Careers Seminar Series
Global Energy Markets
Operations Strategy
Financial Crises in History
Corporate Social Responsibility

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Global Energy Markets
Operations Strategy
Financial Crises in History
Corporate Social Responsibility

Are the ones I would recommend. Definitely stay away from Financial Statement Analysis as the work load is very heavy and the exam is very difficult. Most students at Nova do not recommend it, and it was definitely a mistake that I attended the course. However, if you are very interested in balance sheet, income statements and forecasts you will learn a lot from the course.

questions.answer: There were no unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Alcohol and going to restaurants are very cheap compared to what I expected.
Grocery shopping is a bit cheaper than in Denmark in general, but still more expensive than anticipated.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The Nova Student Union arranged many different events and trips that students could attend.
E.g. trips to the Azore Islands, surf trips to the best surf places in the world etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I attended a weekend surf trip for 200 Euros with everything paid for which I could definitely recommend. It is mostly other exchange students and then the student union so everyone is open and are there for the same reasons. 
The various trips in general to different places I could recommend, especially for meeting new people and I recommend doing it at the start of the semester to meet as many people as possible.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to the city of Sintra (when it's not tourist season) - very beautiful place with big castles and palaces. However, there are too many tourists during high peak season and everything costs money to see. 
Go to the Algarve coast for a weekend - I would recommend renting a house by the beach or in the city of Lagos or Albufeira. 
Go to Porto, a bit like Lisbon but smaller and less touristy. 
Go to Madeira or the Azore Islands - pretty cheap flights and they look like Hawaii. 
Try surfing - at Lisbon Surf Camp in Carcavelos, Nova students get 12 surf opportunities (wet suit and surf board) a month for about 50 euros with 4 lessons from professionals.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
The Portugese are generally very slow and relaxed, therefore it can be a bit frustrating for as it seems sort of incompetent sometimes. 
However, the people of Portugal are very open and friendly and generally very good at English, so you will feel very welcome by everyone, and they all want to talk and learn.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk with the ones assigned to your group in class and attend Nova Student Union events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Portugal seems very inefficient, which took some time to get used to as everything was very slow. 
Get used to everything starting 30-60 minutes after the scheduled time.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Very welcoming and open culture, which was very appreciated coming from an exchange student from Denmark. They are very friendly.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Look for apartments early and use the app idealista. Look for apartments in either Bairro Alto (the party area) or Chiado (the best food and drinks and very beautiful - also right next to Bairro Alto). Both areas are close to the train station and metro. I do not recommend living in a place where you a dependant on taking the bus as they are very inconvenient. However, the metro is very good. 
Get the monthly metro card for 40 euros each month through Nova, also works for trains and bus. You need to take the train from the station Cais do Sodre to get to Nova. 
Be very engaged in events with other exchange students and students in general. Will make your stay more enjoyable and will get many experiences.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There are many nice areas to live in in Lisbon, but make sure to choose an area that is close to the metro. 
There is a gym on campus that also has gyms in Lisbon and you can acces them all. 
Try to pool your classes together so you don't have them spread out on all days of the week, as they are usually only 1,5-2 hours long, and you spend a total of about 1,5 hours of transportation each day.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of new people from different countries was definitely one of the best things about my experience as well as living in a different culture and country that is so open and friendly towards foreigners.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Not having the same network of friends and people you know, especially at university where you can ask for help on choosing courses, where to find previous exams, getting notes etc. 
You are very much on your own unless you get to know someone.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
